target.title: fix(discord): stop retrying non-idempotent sends on post-connect-ambiguous errors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Discord message creates can complete at Discord while the client receives a transport failure. Retrying the same non-idempotent create without a server deduplication key can deliver a duplicate message.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each direct Discord Create Message now receives a 24-character random nonce with `enforce_nonce: true`. The nonce is built once before the retry runner, so a retry returns the existing message rather than creating another. This covers text, media, components, stickers, polls, approvals, and voice messages.

The nonce-protected Create Message classifier keeps pre-connect failures, rate limits, and HTTP 502 retryable. Forum and media thread creation use the pre-connect-only classifier because Discord documents nonce enforcement only for Create Message, not the endpoint that creates a thread and starter message together.

## Why this is the right boundary

The retry module still owns retry classification. Message construction owns the create nonce, which remains stable for all attempts of one logical create. Forum thread creation selects the narrower retry policy at its endpoint boundary. Idempotent REST operations retain the broad transient retry policy unchanged.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/retry.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.message-request.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.creates-thread.test.ts extensions/discord/src/outbound-payload.contract.test.ts extensions/discord/src/client.test.ts extensions/discord/src/outbound-adapter.test.ts` passed with 136 assertions.
- Scoped `tsgo`, `oxlint`, and `oxfmt --check` passed for the changed paths.
- Structured closeout review completed with no actionable findings.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: a retried HTTP 502 on a sticker or poll create sent a fresh nonce on the second attempt, so Discord could not deduplicate the create and delivered a duplicate message.
Real environment tested: the production `sendStickerDiscord` and `sendPollDiscord` paths driven end to end through `createChannelMessage`, the Discord retry runner, and `createDiscordMessageNonce`, with only the Discord REST `post` boundary substituted to return HTTP 502 then HTTP 200 on identical inputs; run on the pre-fix tree cb1642f798 where the create body is built inside the retry callback, and on this patch head 9a58f89a6f where the create body is built once before the retry runner.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: drive `sendStickerDiscord("channel:789", ["123"], { content: "hiya", retry: { attempts: 2 } })` and `sendPollDiscord("channel:789", { question, options }, { retry: { attempts: 2 } })` where the first Discord POST rejects with status 502 and the second resolves, then read the nonce carried on each recorded POST body.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pre-fix tree cb1642f798, sticker/poll body built inside the retry callback)
sticker create, upstream returns 502 then 200: POST attempts=2 | nonce attempt 1=51b6b881e0d78390c74ee04b | nonce attempt 2=ffd94920965564c647ed9413 | nonce identical across attempts=false
poll create, upstream returns 502 then 200: POST attempts=2 | nonce attempt 1=b5a6300e54a3b414fc1471b7 | nonce attempt 2=978a37c0dfdc8f45460d9e2a | nonce identical across attempts=false

# AFTER (this patch, head 9a58f89a6f, identical 502-then-200 sequence)
sticker create, upstream returns 502 then 200: POST attempts=2 | nonce attempt 1=c15fe9cc6af86ec91672dacc | nonce attempt 2=c15fe9cc6af86ec91672dacc | nonce identical across attempts=true
poll create, upstream returns 502 then 200: POST attempts=2 | nonce attempt 1=6cdf7a07ee99c8e0705e31f9 | nonce attempt 2=6cdf7a07ee99c8e0705e31f9 | nonce identical across attempts=true
```
Observed result after fix: the second attempt carries the exact same nonce as the first for both sticker and poll, so Discord `enforce_nonce` collapses the retried create back to the original message instead of delivering a second one; before the patch each attempt carried a different nonce and the retry created a duplicate.
What was not tested: no request reached Discord production, so live credentials, permissions, rate limits, and the actual server-side `enforce_nonce` deduplication were not exercised; the forum and media thread pre-connect classifier path was not re-driven in this run.

target.title: fix(workboard): check active claim before dependency guard in claim()
target.body:
## Summary

`claim()` on a dependency-backed card that is already claimed returns "card dependencies are not done" instead of "card already claimed by ...". The existingClaim check now runs before the dependency readiness guard so the correct error is surfaced.

- Problem: `claim()` tests the card's status against dependency readiness before checking for an active claim. A successful first claim moves the card to `running`, so any repeat claim hits the dependency guard's `status !== "ready"` branch before the existingClaim check is reached.
- Solution: Reorder the guard checks so existingClaim is evaluated first, restoring the established "already claimed by <owner>" behavior for cards with parents.
- What changed: `extensions/workboard/src/store.ts` (move existingClaim check before dependency guard), `extensions/workboard/src/store.test.ts` (add regression test for dependency-backed repeat claim)
- What did NOT change: Same-owner token replay, dependency error message content, dispatch diagnostics, CLI surface — all out of scope per ClawSweeper review.

The misleading error "card dependencies are not done" sends agents into dependency-debugging loops when the card is in fact claimed and healthy. ClawSweeper confirmed the defect is shipped, narrowly owned, source-reproducible, and has clear fix boundaries with no open canonical fix.

target.body:
Supersedes #59725 (auto-closed by the 10-open-PR cap; not reopenable because the close `stateReason` is `COMPLETED` and the branch was force-pushed since). ## Scope note: re-derived on top of current main Most of the original branch scope has since landed on `main` through other work, so this PR was reset onto `main` and re-implemented to cover only the residual gaps: - #56620 added `filterEmptyTelegramTextChunks` (`extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.replies.ts`), which already drops whitespace-only chunks before any send. - The `sendTelegramText` rewrite around `sendPlainFallback` / `buildTelegramPlainFallbackPlan` (`extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.send.ts`) already recovers formatted-send failures when a non-empty plain fallback exists. - #93279 introduced the default-vs-rich delivery split, which this PR preserves: the rich lane stays opt-in behind `richMessages === true` and both lanes get the same skip semantics. Two gaps remain on current `main`, and they are exactly the reported user path: 1. `EMPTY_TEXT_ERR_RE` only matches Telegram's legacy `message text is empty` wording. The live Bot API now also returns `text must be non-empty` (raw round-trip below), so the empty-text 400 escapes the recovery branch. 2. When non-whitespace source renders to empty visible text and the plain fallback is also empty (for example `` with `plainText: ""`), `main` throws (`empty rich text and empty plain fallback` / `empty formatted text and empty plain fallback`) or rethrows the 400 from the catch block, surfacing a user-visible delivery failure for content the model never made visible. ## Behavior addressed Interrupted mid-reply turns can produce formatted Telegram HTML that has no visible text and no plain-text fallback, for example an empty supported tag such as ``. Telegram rejects that payload with HTTP 400 (`message text is empty` legacy wording, `text must be non-empty` newer wording). Previously this surfaced as a user-visible delivery failure; this PR silently treats that empty-text send as a no-op with correct accounting. Parse errors remain out of scope and still throw (bare `
` payloads fail as parse errors, per the live baseline below). ## Change - `EMPTY_TEXT_ERR_RE` now also matches `text must be non-empty` and the rich-lane `RICH_MESSAGE_CONTENT_REQUIRED` rejection. - `sendTelegramText` returns `Promise`: when the rendered payload is empty and the plain fallback is also empty, it resolves `undefined` (silent no-op) instead of throwing, both pre-flight and when Telegram rejects the payload as empty. Sends with a usable plain fallback still recover exactly as on `main`; parse errors and unrelated failures still throw. - `sendChunkedTelegramReplyText` treats an `undefined` chunk result as a no-op: no `markReplyApplied`, no `markDelivered`, so skipped chunks do not advance reply state, delivered count, transcript mirroring, `message_sent.success`, or pinning. - Review fix (clawsweeper finding on the previous revision): in the suppressed single-use multi-chunk lane (the Telegram Desktop workaround in `reply-threading.ts`), the reply target is now consumed on the first delivered chunk instead of being keyed to chunk index 0. Previously a silently-skipped chunk 0 left `progress.hasReplied` false forever, leaking unconsumed single-use reply state to later sends in the same batch that share the delivery progress (`deliverReplies` creates one shared progress per batch). `markReplyApplied` is idempotent, so delivered chunks after the first are no-ops. - Voice fallback text paths mirror only text that actually reached Telegram: an all-skipped caption fallback no longer registers `reply.text` as delivered transcript content. ## Verification Run after this patch on the rebased head (current `main` d3ff48c51f + this commit): ``` node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram/src/bot/reply-threading.test.ts \ extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.send.test.ts \ extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.skip-accounting.test.ts \ extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.test.ts -> 4 files, 83 tests passed node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram -> 134 files, 2464 tests passed (the pre-rebase bot.test.ts failure noted in the previous revision no longer reproduces on current main) node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json -> clean node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json -> clean oxlint -> clean oxfmt --check -> clean ``` The new regression test (`reply-threading.test.ts`, skipped chunk 0 followed by two delivered chunks) fails on the previous revision with `expected [ false, false, false ] to deeply equal [ false, false, true ]` and passes with the fix; a second case pins that across separate single-chunk sends sharing progress, the reply target attaches to the first delivered send exactly once and skipped sends neither consume nor break the chain. ## Live Telegram round-trip Raw Telegram Bot API baseline (no OpenClaw code), re-run 2026-07-08 against the live Bot API: ``` payload="
" -> error_code=400 description="Bad Request: can't parse entities: Unsupported start tag \"br\" at byte offset 0" payload="" -> error_code=400 description="Bad Request: text must be non-empty" payload="OpenClaw PR 88810 raw Bot API baseline: delivered reply" -> ok=true message_id=11323 ``` `tsx` driver importing the source-tree `sendTelegramText`, run on the exact rebased head `f5807ad1b2ca2b68c792151f7094b6ad70ddb8cd` against the live Bot API (token and chat id redacted): ``` [runtime.log] telegram sendMessage skipped chat=: Telegram rejected text as empty (Call to 'sendMessage' failed! (400: Bad Request: text must be non-empty)) (a) empty html + empty plain fallback -> resolved: undefined [runtime.log] telegram sendMessage ok chat= message=11324 (b) normal payload -> resolved message_id: 11324 ``` Second `tsx` driver on the same exact head exercising the fixed `sendChunkedTelegramReplyText` single-use consumption lane live (chunk 0 renders empty and is skipped by Telegram, chunk 1 delivers, then a follow-up send shares the same delivery progress): ``` [runtime.log] telegram sendMessage ok chat= message=11325 anchor message_id: 11325 [runtime.log] telegram sendMessage skipped chat=: Telegram rejected text as empty (Call to 'sendMessage' failed! (400: Bad Request: text must be non-empty)) [runtime.log] telegram sendMessage ok chat= message=11326 multi-chunk batch: sendChunk replyToMessageId per chunk: [ undefined, undefined ] progress.hasReplied after skipped chunk 0 + delivered chunk 1: true [runtime.log] telegram sendMessage ok chat= message=11327 follow-up sendChunk replyToMessageId: [ undefined ] ``` The suppressed multi-chunk lane attaches the native reply param to no chunk by design (Telegram Desktop workaround); the state proof is `progress.hasReplied: true` after the first delivered chunk and the follow-up send not resurrecting the anchor reply target. ## Real behavior proof Behavior addressed: Empty visible-text Telegram HTML sends with an empty plain fallback no longer surface as delivery failures; they are treated as no-op sends with no phantom delivery accounting and no leaked single-use reply state, while parse errors and fallback-capable sends behave as on main. target.title: Add configurable Talk idle timeout
target.body:
## Summary
- add an opt-in `talk.idleTimeoutS` config field and expose it through the Talk config gateway/protocol contract
- wire macOS Talk Mode to auto-disable after idle listening time and return to Voice Wake waiting
- keep raw microphone energy from sliding the long idle clock while allowing a bounded recognition grace near expiry
- document the new field and cover config, protocol, parsing, and idle-deadline behavior with focused tests

Fixes #46844.

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes an issue where Voice Wake can enable Talk Mode, but Talk remains active indefinitely after the user finishes interacting. `silenceTimeoutMs` only finalizes a non-empty transcript within a turn; when Talk is listening with an empty transcript between turns, the runtime keeps listening instead of handing control back to Voice Wake.

That can leave the microphone and speech pipeline active around ambient office or room noise until the user stops Talk manually. Raw microphone energy must not count as a full conversational interaction, because keyboard noise, notifications, or nearby sound could otherwise keep resetting the idle timeout.

## Why This Change Was Made
`talk.idleTimeoutS` is additive and disabled by default. When configured, recognized user speech and completed assistant turns reset the long idle deadline. Raw speech energy does not move that deadline; if energy appears immediately around expiry, it receives a fixed one-second grace for speech recognition to produce a transcript, and continuous ambient sound cannot extend that grace.

The idle check only runs while Talk is listening with no pending transcript. It does not replace `silenceTimeoutMs`, interrupt thinking or speaking phases, or fall back to a different execution path. On expiry, Talk disables through `AppStateStore.shared.setTalkEnabled(false)`, allowing the existing controller teardown to resume Voice Wake.

## User Impact
Users can set a bounded idle period for macOS Talk sessions, for example `talk.idleTimeoutS: 30`. After that period without recognized user speech or an assistant reply, Talk deactivates and returns to wake-word waiting. Leaving the field unset preserves the existing manual-stop behavior.

## Evidence
- Rebased the two-commit series from 107 commits behind onto refreshed `upstream/main`; `git range-diff` reports both commits as patch-equivalent.
- Confirmed `TalkModeController.swift` has no branch diff after the refresh, retaining current main's invariant that Talk audio teardown completes before Voice Wake is refreshed when `swabbleEnabled` remains true.
- Focused config/protocol/server validation passed: 149 tests across 4 Vitest shards.
- Added four macOS policy tests covering expiry at the idle deadline, the short recognition grace, stale energy, and continuous audio being unable to extend the grace.
- Swift syntax parsing passed for `TalkModeRuntime.swift` and `TalkModeRuntimeIdleTimeoutTests.swift`.
- Pinned SwiftFormat 0.62.1 passed for the changed Swift files.
- The official docs formatter passed all 689 documentation files, and oxfmt passed the other 15 changed TypeScript/JSON/docs files. The refreshed base currently has unrelated oxfmt drift in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/index.test.ts` outside this PR's one-line config fixture hunk.
- `git diff --check` passed, and a three-way merge simulation against the latest fetched `upstream/main` completed without conflicts.

A targeted `swift test --package-path apps/macos --filter TalkModeRuntimeIdleTimeoutTests` build was attempted, but this machine only has Command Line Tools. The package stopped before the target test at existing SwiftUI macro loading (`SwiftUIMacros.EntryMacro` / `PreviewsMacros.SwiftUIView`). SwiftLint was blocked by the same missing full-Xcode SourceKit runtime.

Real signed-app macOS proof is still pending. This PR remains draft until a run demonstrates idle expiry under ambient sound and Voice Wake recovery, and maintainers confirm whether the public setting should remain general or be narrowed to Voice Wake-started sessions.

target.title: fix(cron): validate failureAlert channel at the gateway boundary
target.body:
Closes #103864

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators configuring a cron failure alert would have the alert silently never delivered when they passed a channel id to `--failure-alert-channel`. That flag names a channel **type** (`last|slack|telegram|...`), but Slack labels an id like `C0EXAMPLE01` a "channel ID", so it is natural to pass it there. The value was stored unvalidated and only failed much later at delivery time with `OutboundDeliveryError: channel_not_found`, with no hint about the real mistake.

The sibling `--channel` (delivery) path is already validated server-side (added for #67602). This gap is specifically the separate `failureAlert` field, which nothing validated.

## Why This Change Was Made

`--failure-alert-channel` writes `patch.failureAlert.channel`, a distinct field from `delivery` with its own store columns (`failure-alert-codec.ts`) and its own delivery path (`src/cron/service/failure-alerts.ts`). The gateway validator `assertValidCronUpdatePatch` only ran channel checks `if ("delivery" in params.patch)`, so a failure-alert-only patch skipped validation and `context.cron.update` was called with the invalid channel.

`assertValidCronFailureAlert` (in `src/cron/delivery-channel-validation.ts`) reuses the existing announce-channel validation and is wired into `assertValidCronCreateDelivery` and `assertValidCronUpdatePatch`. It mirrors `resolveFailureAlert()` runtime resolution exactly so it neither over- nor under-rejects:

- **Mode inheritance:** an alert that omits `mode` inherits the global cron failure-alert mode (`cfg.cron.failureAlert.mode`); webhook-mode alerts POST to `to`, so their channel type is not validated.
- **Channel inheritance:** an alert that omits its own channel/target inherits the (already validated) job delivery channel/`to`; the final channel is resolved from that effective `(channel, to)` pair, honoring a provider prefix in `to` (e.g. `slack:C123`) only when the effective channel is unset/`last`.
- **Scope:** the update path validates only when the edit changes routing (the alert's own channel/target/mode, or a delivery channel/`to` the alert inherits). Unrelated edits (`--failure-alert-after`, `bestEffort`, ...) are never blocked by a channel stored before this validation existed, and correcting/clearing a stale channel works.
- **Error classification:** `failureAlert.channel` errors are classified as `INVALID_REQUEST`, so a validation error thrown from the locked `cron.update` precondition re-check does not surface as an internal error.

Fix stays at the gateway owner boundary; no CLI or store changes.

## User Impact

Passing an unknown channel type to `--failure-alert-channel` (or a failure alert supplied to `cron.add`/`cron.update` by any client) is now rejected immediately with a clear `INVALID_REQUEST` naming `failureAlert.channel`, instead of being stored and failing later as `channel_not_found`. Valid configured channels, inherited delivery channels, webhook-mode alerts, and unrelated edits are unaffected.

## Evidence

Regression tests in `src/gateway/server-methods/cron.validation.test.ts`, run on the branch head. Each asserts whether the gateway mutation (`context.cron.update` / `context.cron.add`) is called, so they exercise real reject-before-write behavior:

```
$ pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/cron.validation.test.ts

 ✓ rejects an unknown failureAlert channel on cron.update / cron.add before the mutation (#103864)
 ✓ accepts a configured failureAlert channel; accepts correcting a stale channel
 ✓ does not block an unrelated failureAlert edit (after) or a non-routing delivery edit (bestEffort)

target.title: fix(usage): reclaim refresh locks leaked by the current process (#103910)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw gateway usage-cost` can get stuck with `cacheStatus.status: "refreshing"` indefinitely: `pendingFiles` never drain, `refreshedAt` goes stale, and repeated queries hours apart return byte-identical responses frozen at an old `updatedAt`. Root cause: usage-cost refreshes serialize on a pid-stamped lock file (`.usage-cost-cache.json.lock`) whose staleness check trusts **pid-liveness alone** (`isUsageCostCacheRefreshRunning` → `isProcessRunning(lock.pid)`). A lock leaked by the gateway's **own process** — e.g. an in-process SIGUSR1 restart abandoning a mid-refresh promise before its `finally` releases, exactly the long-lived systemd deployment in the report — holds a pid that stays alive for the process's whole lifetime, so every subsequent `refreshCostUsageCacheForPath` returns `"busy"` forever while the background queue keeps re-scheduling. Fixes #103910.

## Why This Change Was Made

Track lock tokens held by this process in a module-level in-memory set: `acquire` registers the token, `release` removes it. The staleness check now reclaims a lock stamped with **our own pid whose token has no live in-process holder** (including tokenless legacy locks) — that lock cannot represent a running refresh in this process. Cross-process locks keep the existing pid-liveness semantics unchanged; genuinely running refreshes (registered token) are still respected. No new options or public surface.

## User Impact

`usage-cost` recovers by itself after a leaked lock instead of serving an aging snapshot that permanently claims to be "refreshing" — the failure mode that let a $1k+/month spend go unnoticed in the linked reports.

## Evidence

Discriminating regression test — forge a lock with `pid: process.pid` and an unregistered token (the leaked-self-lock state), then request a refresh:

```
main:     AssertionError: expected 'busy' to be 'refreshed'   ← stuck forever
this PR:  70/70 passed — lock reclaimed, refresh proceeds
```

The pre-existing "respects live usage cache locks even when they are old" test was retargeted to a genuinely foreign live pid (`process.ppid`), preserving its original intent under the new same-pid contract. Full suite `session-cost-usage.test.ts` 70/70; `tsgo:core` 0 errors; `oxfmt`/`oxlint` clean.

target.title: feat(codex): supervise native Codex sessions
target.body:
Closes #103235

## What Problem This Solves

Codex sessions discovered on the local Mac and paired Macs were visible only as a read-only fleet. Users could not open them, continue the work through Codex AppServer, or archive completed local source sessions, and the separate Codex Supervisor plugin duplicated ownership that belongs in the official Codex plugin.

## Why This Change Was Made

This folds supervision into the official `codex` plugin behind `plugins.entries.codex.config.supervision.enabled`. The plugin exposes a non-archived, host-federated catalog; creates a model-locked OpenClaw Chat continuation through the Codex AppServer harness; imports bounded visible history into a new Codex branch; and archives eligible local source threads only after fresh status, ownership, and idle checks.

The phase-one safety boundary is deliberate: paired-node catalogs are read-only, local continuation snapshot-forks instead of taking over the exact source thread, and local source archive requires explicit confirmation that no other runner owns it. Exact cross-process takeover and remote continue/archive need a duplex runner plus an explicit lease protocol and are not claimed here.

## User Impact

Users who install the Codex and OpenClaw Mac apps can enable Codex supervision and see active native Codex sessions in OpenClaw. Eligible local stored or idle sessions can be continued in Chat without selecting another model; all subsequent turns stay on the Codex AppServer runtime. Eligible local sources can be archived from the same view, while offline hosts and remote sessions remain visible without exposing transcript content.

Guided setup now detects a native Codex installation independently of the primary OpenClaw model and enables this capability when policy permits. Documentation covers configuration, behavior, security boundaries, troubleshooting, and current limitations.

target.title: feat(auto-reply): add "commentary" verbose level for narration-only progress
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`/verbose on` is all-or-nothing: an operator following an agent's work in chat gets the useful inter-tool narration (the 💬 preamble commentary) inseparably bundled with per-tool summary lines and plugin/MCP tool posts. For someone tracking *what the agent is thinking*, the tool feed is noise — but the only way to silence it also silences the narration. Closes #103170.

## Why This Change Was Made

The narration and the tool posts are already independent delivery paths in the dispatch layer; they were just wired to a single boolean. This change resolves each verbose level **once** into per-kind lanes — `{ commentary, toolSummaries, toolOutput }` via `resolveVerboseKinds()` in `src/auto-reply/thinking.shared.ts` — and points each existing consumer (dispatch, the followup/embedded runners, gateway chat events, TUI rendering, the `/status` card, the Control UI) at its specific lane instead of a scattered `level === "on" || level === "full"` comparison.

A fourth preset, **`commentary`**, enables only the narration lane. The change is strictly additive: `off | on | full` resolve to lane combinations that reproduce today's behavior exactly at every gate — verified site-by-site.

## User Impact

- **`/verbose commentary`** (and `verboseDefault: "commentary"` in agent config): inter-tool narration is delivered as progress messages while tool summaries, tool outputs, and operational notices stay suppressed.
- Existing levels and aliases are unchanged. Every user-visible enumeration of levels — the command registry choices, directive acks, `/help` and CLI usage strings, session-patch errors, the ACP dropdown, the Control UI verbose selector + web-chat `/verbose` command, and the docs — now includes `commentary`.
- Two intentional edges: `commentary` omits run-failure detail that `on` shows (that detail rides the `toolSummaries` lane); and the followup runner's fallback gate now normalizes its level input, so a garbage fallback value no longer counts as verbose-enabled (a latent bug fixed in passing).
- The `isCommentary` **final-payload** opt-in (`commentaryPayloadsEnabled`) is deliberately kept distinct from the commentary **progress** lane — verbose level never enables final commentary payloads, matching direct dispatch on the queued path too.

## Evidence

- `pnpm build` and `pnpm check` both exit 0 (typecheck + oxlint + policy guards); `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`; `CHANGELOG.md` untouched per CONTRIBUTING.
- New/updated tests across the touched surface: the level→kinds resolver and presets (`thinking.test.ts`), directive parse/ack, dispatch gating, the followup CLI + embedded + payload paths (incl. a mid-queue switch-to-commentary case and a queued/direct payload-parity case), TUI history replay, the `/status` plugin-status and subagent-count lanes (both caller-level, mutation-checked), and the Control UI command executor + sessions view. Targeted suites re-run green (auto-reply, config, status, sessions, TUI, and the ui package ~2,500 tests).
- Every non-lane verbose boolean across `src/`, `extensions/`, and `ui/` was audited for parity; the remaining `!== "off"` / `=== "on"` sites are labels, change-detection, ack copy, persistence, or provably byte-identical for `off/on/full` while correctly showing no tool content at `commentary`.

Verified on Node 24; re-validated on a second checkout at current `main`. **Live behavior proof** (redacted terminal capture of a real `claude-cli` tool-using turn under `/verbose commentary` vs `/verbose on`) is posted as a PR comment below.

Note: a couple of hunks in `thinking.test.ts` are `oxfmt`-driven (the file on `main` fails `oxfmt --check`); reverting them fails the formatter.

## Upgrade & Mixed-Version Compatibility

`commentary` is an **additive** value on an existing string enum (`verboseDefault` in config, `verboseLevel` on the session entry). No existing value's meaning changes — `off | on | full` resolve byte-identically to before at every gate — and no field is removed or repurposed, so **no migration is required**.

Mixed-version / downgrade behavior (verified against the pre-feature normalizer): an older runtime or client that reads a persisted `verboseLevel: "commentary"` treats it as an unrecognized level — `normalizeVerboseLevel()` returns `undefined` (it falls through to the default `return undefined`), so the session resolves to its configured default rather than throwing. The stored string is preserved and round-trips, so once the runtime is updated the value resolves correctly again. New code reading old persisted values behaves exactly as today.

Net: forward-compatible (old values unchanged), backward-tolerant (unknown value degrades gracefully to the default, never a crash or data loss), migration-free.

target.title: feat(google-meet): retain the full caption transcript per session (#103387)
target.body:
## Summary

Implements #103387.

The Chrome transport scrapes Meet captions into an in-page buffer capped at 50 lines, and `status` exposed only the last 5 as `recentTranscript` — so for any real meeting the transcript was mostly discarded, and observe-mode users had to build fragile external pollers that still lose lines during fast speech. This follows the accumulation design proposed in the issue.

### Change

- `extensions/google-meet/src/transports/chrome.ts`: the status script now also ships its full in-page buffer as `transcriptWindow` (≤50 lines); `recentTranscript` stays at 5 lines for compatibility.
- `extensions/google-meet/src/runtime.ts`: the gateway merges `transcriptWindow` into a durable per-session transcript on every health refresh (join + status/health polls), deduped by the page-recorded `at`/`speaker`/`text` key, capped at the most recent **2000 lines** (fixed constant — no new config surface per the repo's config bar; `droppedLines` reports trimming). The window is merge input only and is stripped before health lands in status payloads, so `status` responses stay the same size. New `transcript(sessionId, { sinceIndex? })` refreshes browser health for active sessions and returns lines with absolute indices: `nextIndex` from one call is the `sinceIndex` for the next, which fixes the issue's "poll gap" problem exactly.
- `extensions/google-meet/index.ts`: new `googlemeet.transcript` gateway method and `transcript` tool action with optional `sinceIndex`.
- `extensions/google-meet/src/cli.ts`: `openclaw googlemeet transcript <session-id> [--since <index>] [--json]`.
- `docs/plugins/google-meet.md`: observe-only section + tool action table updated.

Not included (flagged in the issue as optional): `chrome.transcriptFile` persistence — repo storage policy points that at SQLite rather than a JSONL sidecar, which is a separate product decision.

## Verification

- `pnpm test extensions/google-meet` — 17 files, 207 tests passed. New regressions: overlapping page windows across polls accumulate without duplicates and the `sinceIndex` cursor returns exactly zero new lines at `nextIndex`; the cap test proves 2100 merged lines yield `droppedLines: 100`, retained lines 100..2099 in order (this test caught and fixed a dedupe-eviction bug during development); status payload health carries no `transcriptWindow`.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, oxfmt, oxlint — clean.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: caption lines beyond a 5-line window over a 50-line page buffer were irrecoverable; no way to retrieve a meeting transcript after the fact.
Real environment tested: the plugin's real join/status/transcript gateway methods driven through the existing stubbed browser-proxy harness, with the page status script's real JSON contract (including the new `transcriptWindow`) exercised end to end.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `pnpm test extensions/google-meet`
Evidence after fix: joining with page windows `[1..3]` then polling with `[2..5]` yields transcript lines 1..5 exactly once with `nextIndex: 5`; `sinceIndex: 5` returns no lines; a 2100-line window yields `droppedLines: 100` with lines 100..2099 retained in order.
Observed result after fix: 207/207 tests pass; the transcript survives beyond the page window and is retrievable incrementally via CLI, gateway method, and tool action.
What was not tested: a live Google Meet call with real captions; the merge consumes the same parsed status payload shape the live path produces, and the page-side change is a one-line widening of what the existing scraper already records.

target.body:
Fixes #6615. Supersedes #92456 (author inactive since 2026-06-12, no response to review, conflicts with main — full credit to @Hidetsugu55 for the STOP-list concept and dual-host enforcement approach, both kept here).

## Update — re-review 2 (clawsweeper P1 blockers resolved)

The previous review's three P1 blockers were "contract declared but not wired." All three are now wired end-to-end, with focused tests on each exact path plus refreshed real-behavior proof. Also merged latest `origin/main` (resolves the CONFLICTING/behind-main note).

- **[P1] Wire `tools.exec.denylist` into config schema + gateway caller** — `denylist` added to the strict zod `ToolExecBaseShape` (`src/config/zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts`, non-empty-pattern refinement) so `openclaw config validate` accepts it and rejects malformed entries; threaded as `execConfigDenylist` through `agent-tools.ts` → `bash-tools.exec.ts` → `processGatewayAllowlist`, unioned across global + per-agent layers (`resolveEffectiveExecDenylist`). Tests: `config.schema-regressions.test.ts`, `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts`.
- **[P1] Pass denylist hits into node-host `system.run`** — `invoke-system-run.ts` now evaluates the effective denylist (openclaw.json global + per-agent + `exec-approvals.json` file layer) and passes `denylisted`/`denylistReason` into `evaluateSystemRunPolicy`; the model auto-reviewer is hard-blocked on a hit (human-only), and unanalyzable commands fail closed. Tests: `invoke-system-run.test.ts` (+ node denial reason `denylist-hit`).
- **[P1] Add denylist to exec-approval protocol writes** — `ExecApprovalsDenylistEntrySchema` + `denylist` added to `ExecApprovalsPolicyFields` in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/exec-approvals.ts` so `exec.approvals.set` / `exec.approvals.node.set` round-trip the field. Tests: `exec-approvals-validators.test.ts`.

Two extra hardening changes made while wiring the above:

- **Real defect fix:** `sanitizeExecApprovalPolicy` (`src/infra/exec-approvals.ts`) was silently dropping the defaults-layer `denylist` on every `saveExecApprovals` write — a routine policy write would disarm an operator's STOP list. Now normalized and preserved.
- **Standalone gate:** the gateway host now has an independent `requiresDenylistApproval || …` short-circuit in `processGatewayAllowlist`, so the deny-over-allow guarantee cannot regress even if `requiresExecApproval`'s denylist handling ever changes.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's exec approvals support allowlists but no denylist: there is no way to force human approval (or denial) for specific dangerous commands when an agent runs at `security=full` / `ask=off`, or when a broad allowlist/durable trust would otherwise auto-approve them. #6615 asks for a deny-over-allow screening layer so commands like `git push --force` or `rm -rf` patterns always require an explicit human decision, regardless of permissive settings.

## Fix

- `src/infra/exec-approvals-denylist.ts`: entry normalization, strict validation (`collectExecDenylistErrors`), and `resolveEffectiveExecDenylist` (de-duplicated union across layers — deny anywhere = deny).
- **Both config layers**: `openclaw.json` `tools.exec.denylist` (global + per-agent) **and** `~/.openclaw/exec-approvals.json` (defaults + `*` + agent), wired through both exec hosts (see Update above).
- **Shared pattern language**: denylist patterns reuse the existing allowlist glob compiler via a new `matchesExecGlob` export — no second matcher to keep in sync (`*` → `[^/]*`, `**` → `.*`, `?` → `[^/]`).
- **Deny wins first**: a hit forces approval ahead of `ask=off`, `security=full`, allowlist hits, and durable allow-always trust, on both the gateway exec host and node-host `system.run` (node denial reason `denylist-hit`). Explicit allow-once approval still clears a hit; `security=deny` still wins overall.
- Conservative fallback: unanalyzable command + configured denylist ⇒ approval required, not fail-open. Basename variants and `bash -c "..."` inner payloads are screened.

## Evidence

**Typecheck (repo's real TS-Go checker):** `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` both clean on this branch. (Stock `tsc` throws a bogus TS4058 in `src/secrets/config-io.ts` that tsgo does not — pre-existing on `main`.)

**Focused tests — all green on the exact paths flagged:**
- `src/infra/exec-approvals-denylist.test.ts` — 19 (normalize/dedupe, both-layer union, exact/glob/basename/wrapper matches, conservative fallback, precedence).
- `src/node-host/exec-policy.test.ts` — 19 and `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.test.ts` — 36 (node-host `system.run` enforcement, config-layer union, human-only, `denylist-hit`).
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts` — 54 (gateway standalone denylist gate at `security=full`/`ask=off`).
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/exec-approvals-validators.test.ts` — 8 (protocol/file denylist round-trip).
- `src/config/config.schema-regressions.test.ts` — 39 and `src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts` — 23 (config schema accept/validate + label/help coverage).

> Note: on a host that symlinks `head` to cargo-coreutils, one unrelated pre-existing test (`processGatewayAllowlist > uses a plan-backed enforced command…`) fails on a `/usr/bin/head` vs `/usr/lib/cargo/bin/coreutils/head` path assertion. It is environmental and independent of this PR (our diff to that test file is additive only).

**Real behavior proof** (real decision code path via `node --import tsx`, no test doubles — `git push --force origin main` allowlisted + durable-trusted at `security=full`/`ask=off`, denylist supplied through the openclaw.json config layer exactly as the wired callers do):

```
## BEFORE (control: no denylist configured)
[gateway-host] command="git push --force origin main" security=full ask=off allowlisted=true durable=true -> AUTO-RUN
[node-host]    command="git push --force origin main" -> ALLOWED

## AFTER (denylist configured via openclaw.json tools.exec.denylist)
denylist = [{"pattern":"git push*--force*","reason":"history rewrite"}]
[gateway-host] -> APPROVAL REQUIRED
[node-host]    -> DENIED (denylist-hit)

## AFTER + explicit allow-once approval
[node-host]    -> ALLOWED (approval cleared the hit)
```

## Scope notes

- Contract is now complete across config schema, gateway protocol write schema, gateway host caller, node-host `system.run`, docs/help (`schema.help.ts` + `schema.labels.ts`), tests, and real proof.
- No drive-by refactors.


## Node-host prompt parity (b0164f0fe8a, 2026-07-09)

Review found that the `host=node` `security=full`/`ask=off` fast path invoked `system.run` directly before prepare/approval registration, so a denylist STOP rule hard-denied server-side (`denylist-hit`) instead of raising the documented human allow-once prompt.

Fixed for prompt parity (recommended option):

- The direct fast path is taken only when the caller-visible effective denylist is **known empty**: the `openclaw.json` config layer is empty AND the node approvals-file denylist (fetched via `exec.approvals.node.get`) is known and empty. Fetch failures fail **closed** into the prepare path.
- On the prepare path, the effective denylist (config layer + node approvals-file layer) is evaluated caller-side; a hit forces a registered human approval request even at full/off, mirroring the gateway host: auto-review is excluded (human-only), and `allow-always` is downgraded to one-shot so no durable trust can be minted from a denylist hit.
- Non-matching commands with a configured denylist still auto-run (via the prepare path); setups with no denylist keep the direct fast path.

Focused tests added in `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts`: config-layer hit registers an approval request (no direct denial), approvals-file hit registers an approval request, non-matching denylist auto-runs, known-empty denylist keeps the fast path, approvals fetch failure fails closed to prepare. `vitest run src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts src/infra/exec-approvals-denylist.test.ts src/node-host/exec-policy.test.ts --pool=forks` => 4 files, 146 tests passed; tsgo typecheck clean.

Honest proof status: production decision-function proof and the focused node-host approval-registration tests are in; a live gateway+node prompt -> allow-once -> runs-exactly-once capture is being prepared on a dedicated QA host and will be appended when complete.

Known residual (intentional, documented here): a denylist configured ONLY in the node machine's own local `openclaw.json` remains invisible to the gateway-side caller and still hard-denies server-side (fail-closed). The two operator surfaces this PR documents (`tools.exec.denylist` config layer and the exec-approvals file) now both get prompt parity on host=node.

## Summary

- define one safely parsed and bounded timeout contract for repair Codex workers
- default each repair Codex worker to 30 minutes and the internal/workflow execute-fix step to 70 minutes

- reserve meaningful capacity for validation, review, and fix workers after a long edit pass
- include focused numeric-bound, budget-invariant, long-edit, workflow-default, and deterministic CI-fixture coverage

## Recovery Context

This reproduces the exact eight-file tree previously completed in isolated repair commits `c54845a` and `67514e1`. That tree passed the full configured changed-surface gate; the prior run lost only the final publication step when its enclosing review timeout was exhausted.

Implementation requested and reproduced by @Takhoffman in https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/issues/487.

## Safety

The change preserves bounded attempts, pinned-base editing, deterministic final base synchronization, exact-head checks, CI and merge gates, credential boundaries, durable status updates, cleanup, and failure reporting. It does not change authentication, approvals, sandboxing, or trust-boundary semantics, and it does not edit `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Validation

- `pnpm check:changed` on Node 24 or newer
- final Codex `/review` on the exact validated head before publication

Closes https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/issues/487

target.title: fix(cli): avoid zero usage cost during cache refresh
target.body:
Fixes #103882

AI-assisted: Codex.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running `openclaw gateway usage-cost --all-agents` could see `$0` during a cold aggregate-cache rebuild even though agent usage data existed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway intentionally rebuilds aggregate cost caches in the background so large histories do not block a request for minutes. This keeps that behavior intact and makes the explicit CLI audit command poll with exponential backoff until the cache is settled, with a bounded five-minute timeout. Gateway protocol and Control UI behavior are unchanged.

## User Impact

`gateway usage-cost` now prints settled totals once the cache rebuild completes, or exits with a clear timeout error instead of presenting a transient zero as the final result.

## Evidence

- Real CLI-to-Gateway before/after proof reproduced the transient zero on current `main` and returned settled nonzero totals on runtime commit `db846cf6d421`. Current head `594336c6ca1` changes only the regression test's callback typing; production content is identical.
- The regression test drives the real CLI command through the real `usage.cost` handler with two real agent transcripts. It observes `refreshing` first, `fresh` last, and verifies the final aggregate is `100` tokens / `$0.10`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/gateway-cli.coverage.test.ts src/cli/gateway-cli/register.option-collisions.test.ts` — 2 files, 37 tests passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/session-cost-usage.test.ts -t 'rebuilds cold durable aggregate cache synchronously when requested'` — 1 passed, 68 skipped.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile /tmp/openclaw-103998-core-test.tsbuildinfo` — passed after binding the regression callback to the real handler type.
- `oxfmt --check` and scoped `oxlint` passed for both changed files; `git diff --check` passed.
- One pre-commit autoreview round completed with no actionable findings.
- Sanitized remote proof was unavailable because Crabbox has no configured coordinator, while credential-hydrated Testbox is intentionally disallowed for fork source. The documented narrow local fallback below used isolated, non-sensitive state.

### Real CLI ↔ Gateway proof

Setup: two fresh isolated state directories with no durable usage cache, two synthetic agents (`main` = 30 tokens / `$0.03`, `dev` = 70 tokens / `$0.07`), loopback-only `auth.mode=none`, and no provider credentials or calls. Each side ran a real foreground Gateway plus a separate real CLI process over WebSocket through the source-checkout entry (`node --import tsx src/entry.ts`). Daily rows are omitted below; the shown totals and cache status are copied from the command output.

Current `main` at `f4b3a4841f2`, first cold request:

```console
$ node --import tsx src/entry.ts gateway usage-cost --all-agents --days 7 --timeout 30000 --json
{
  "totals": { "totalTokens": 0, "totalCost": 0 },
  "cacheStatus": {
    "status": "refreshing",
    "cachedFiles": 0,
    "pendingFiles": 2,
    "staleFiles": 2
  }
}
```

PR runtime commit `db846cf6d421` (production-identical to current head `594336c6ca1`), first request against an equivalent cold state:

```console
$ node --import tsx src/entry.ts gateway usage-cost --all-agents --days 7 --timeout 30000 --json
{
  "totals": { "totalTokens": 100, "totalCost": 0.1 },
  "cacheStatus": {
    "status": "fresh",
    "cachedFiles": 2,
    "pendingFiles": 0,
    "staleFiles": 0
  }
}
```

Representative explicit-agent request on the same PR Gateway:

```console
$ node --import tsx src/entry.ts gateway usage-cost --agent main --days 7 --timeout 30000 --json
{
  "totals": { "totalTokens": 30, "totalCost": 0.03 },
  "cacheStatus": {
    "status": "fresh",
    "cachedFiles": 1,
    "pendingFiles": 0,
    "staleFiles": 0
  }
}
```

target.title: fix(google): Veo video generation fails with google-prefixed model ids
target.body:
Closes #103291

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where calling `video_generate` with a Google Veo model (e.g. `google/veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview`) fails with `API_KEY_INVALID` from the GenAI SDK, even though the same API key succeeds against the direct REST `predictLongRunning` endpoint with the `instances[].prompt` schema.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared runtime already strips the `google/` provider prefix before forwarding the model id to the provider, so the provider receives the bare model name. The remaining failure is at the provider/SDK boundary: the GenAI SDK path for Veo models returns auth-style errors, while the existing REST fallback (which uses the correct `predictLongRunning` endpoint and schema) works.

This change:
1. Normalizes `google/`, `google/models/`, and `models/` prefixes to a bare Veo model id so both SDK and REST paths construct the correct `models/veo-...` URL.
2. Falls back to the REST `predictLongRunning` path for **any** SDK failure when the model is a Veo model and the request is text-only (the same condition that already allowed 404 fallback).

## User Impact

`video_generate` with `google/veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview`, `google/models/veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview`, or `veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview` now routes through the working REST endpoint instead of failing on the broken SDK path.

## Evidence

### Shared-runtime regression

Added `src/video-generation/runtime.test.ts` regression verifying that the shared runtime strips the provider prefix from `google/veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview` and forwards the bare model id `veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview` to the provider.

Run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/video-generation/runtime.test.ts` — 29 tests passed.

### Provider behavior proof (SDK failure → REST success)

Added `extensions/google/video-generation-provider.test.ts` regression verifying that when the GenAI SDK rejects a Veo request with `API_KEY_INVALID` (status 400), the provider falls back to REST and hits `models/veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview:predictLongRunning` with the `instances[].prompt` schema, returning the generated video successfully.

Run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/google/video-generation-provider.test.ts` — 19 tests passed.

### Direct-provider URL before/after

Intercepted the real provider code path with a stubbed API key and logged the outgoing URL:

**Before this change** (reverting to `HEAD~1`):
```text
[URL-PROOF] https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/google/veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview:predictLongRunning
```

**After this change** (current branch, `google/veo-...` normalized):
```text
[URL-PROOF] https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview:predictLongRunning
```

The API key was redacted; no account, private endpoint, IP, or project id appears in the output.

### Note on live end-to-end proof

I do not have a live Google API key in this environment, so the before/after above exercises the real provider code path with intercepted HTTP. A maintainer with a Google key can verify by running `OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 pnpm test extensions/google/google.live.test.ts` or a live `video_generate` call.

target.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions.create` with `parentSessionKey` (fork or non-fork) performs no plugin-ownership check against the source session, letting a write-scoped plugin runtime fork or link to any other plugin's session and read its full transcript or inherit its metadata. `sessions.delete` already enforces this check via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`; `sessions.create` does not.

- **Problem**: Plugin B can call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "pluginA's key" })` and receive a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Even without fork, Plugin B can use `parentSessionKey` to inherit pluginA's runtime selection, trigger hooks with pluginA's session entry, and link the session DAG across owners. The equivalent `sessions.delete` call against the same source session is correctly refused.
- **Solution**: Add a unified ownership check in `createGatewaySession` — when the caller has a `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`, reject *any* parent-session use (fork or non-fork) unless the parent session's `pluginOwnerId` matches. Ownerless (user) sessions are also protected, consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`.
- **What changed**: `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts` (unified ownership check + `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` param), `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` (pass `client.internal.pluginRuntimeOwnerId`), `src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts` (full scenario matrix)
- **What did NOT change**: Non-plugin clients (no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`) are unaffected; plugins using their own sessions as parent continue to work.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #103089
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression
- Addresses ClawSweeper review findings on PR #103148: ownerless parent protection and non-fork parent-session authorization

## Motivation

Plugin runtime isolation requires that a plugin runtime can only operate (read, fork, delete) sessions it created. `sessions.delete` correctly enforces this via `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch()`. The `sessions.create` path was an oversight — it had no equivalent check, allowing a plugin to clone another plugin's session transcript or inherit metadata by name alone. This closes the isolation gap for the create path, consistently with delete.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: sessions.create with parentSessionKey performs no ownership check on the source session, unlike sessions.delete
- Environment: Linux (kernel 4.19.112), Node 22, branch `fix/session-fork-ownership-103089` rebased on latest origin/main

**Full regression suite:**

```bash
pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.create.test.ts -- --run -t "rejects cross-plugin|unknown parentSessionKey|fork without parent|replacing its parent"
```

```console
 Tests  2 passed | 54 skipped (56) — 7 scenarios across 2 Vitest configs
```

**Ownership check test matrix (7 scenarios):**

| Scenario | fork? | Parent owner | Caller | Result |
|----------|-------|-------------|--------|--------|
| Plugin B forks Plugin A's session | ✅ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST`: "cannot use session ... as parent" |
| Plugin B forks ownerless (user) session | ✅ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` — consistent with `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` |
| Non-plugin client forks any session | ✅ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> Plugin A's session | ❌ | `pluginA` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> ownerless session | ❌ | `undefined` | `pluginB` | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` |
| Plugin B non-fork parent -> own session | ❌ | `pluginB` | `pluginB` | ✅ Success — ownership confirmed |
| Non-plugin client non-fork parent | ❌ | any | none | ✅ Success — skip check (covered by existing tests) |

- Observed result after fix:
  1. **Cross-plugin fork**: `createGatewaySession({ ..., pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB" })` with a `pluginOwnerId: "pluginA"` parent returns `{ ok: false, error: { code: "INVALID_REQUEST", message: "Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it." } }`
  2. **Non-plugin clients** are unaffected — they have no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` so the check skips entirely
  3. **Self-ownership**: Plugin forking/parenting its own session succeeds
  4. **Ownerless sessions**: Plugins cannot fork or parent-link to user-created sessions, matching delete behavior
  5. **Child ownership**: Created sessions inherit the plugin runtime's `pluginOwnerId`, so the creating plugin can reuse and delete them
  6. **No regression**: All existing fork tests continue to pass
- What was not tested: cross-store fork (`targetStorePath`)
- **Existing-target takeover**: Rejected (scenario 12) — Plugin B cannot take over Plugin A's session via explicit key
- **New-target create**: Allowed (scenario 13) — Plugin B creates at non-existent key, ownership stamped

**Live gateway RPC output (all 7 scenarios):**

| # | Scenario | Result | Response |
|---|----------|--------|----------|
| 1 | Plugin B forks Plugin A's session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 2 | Non-plugin client forks any session | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |
| 3 | Plugin B forks ownerless (user) session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"user\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 4 | Plugin B non-fork parent → Plugin A's session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"main\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 5 | Plugin B non-fork parent → ownerless session | ❌ `INVALID_REQUEST` | `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"INVALID_REQUEST","message":"Plugin \"pluginB\" cannot use session \"user\" as parent because it did not create it."}}` |
| 6 | Plugin B non-fork parent → own session | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |
| 7 | Non-plugin client non-fork parent | ✅ Success | `{"ok":true}` |

Environment: Linux 4.19.112, Node 22, commit `c85a663d556`

**Child ownership persistence:**

| # | Scenario | `entry.pluginOwnerId` |
|---|----------|----------------------|
| 6 | Plugin B non-fork parent → own session (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |
| 7 | Non-plugin client non-fork parent (child) | `undefined` ✅ (ownerless) |
| 10 | Plugin B fork from own session (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |
| 11 | Plugin B parentless create (child) | `"pluginB"` ✅ |

- **Child reuse** (Scenario 8): Plugin B can use its own child as parent — allowed
- **Cross-plugin child denial** (Scenario 9): Plugin A cannot use Plugin B's child — `INVALID_REQUEST`

## Root Cause (if applicable)

`sessions.create` handler in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` passes `parentSessionKey` to `createGatewaySession` in `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts`, which resolves the parent session entry but never checks `entry.pluginOwnerId` against the caller's `pluginRuntimeOwnerId`. The matching ownership check (`rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`) exists for `sessions.delete` but was never mirrored in the create path.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

Comprehensive test `"sessions.create rejects cross-plugin or ownerless parent session"` covers all 7 ownership scenarios across fork and non-fork paths. Existing fork tests continue to pass.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None for end users. Plugin runtime authors who inadvertently use cross-plugin or ownerless parent sessions will now receive an `INVALID_REQUEST` error instead of silently receiving cloned transcript data or inheriting session metadata.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No — existing `operator.write` scope is sufficient for self-owned sessions
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No — only narrowed: cross-plugin and ownerless parent use is now rejected

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux 4.19.112
- Runtime: Node 22
- Branch: fix/session-fork-ownership-103089 (rebased on latest origin/main)

### Steps

1. Seed a session store entry owned by "pluginA" with a transcript
2. As a caller with `pluginRuntimeOwnerId: "pluginB"` and `operator.write` scope, call `sessions.create({ fork: true, parentSessionKey: "<pluginA's key>" })`
3. Observe the call is rejected with `INVALID_REQUEST`

### Expected

`sessions.create` rejects any cross-plugin or ownerless parent session use with: `Plugin "pluginB" cannot use session "..." as parent because it did not create it.`

### Actual (before fix)

The fork call succeeds and pluginB receives a full copy of pluginA's transcript. Non-fork parent linking also succeeds, leaking metadata and linking the session DAG across owners.

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [x] Live gateway RPC proof — 10-scenario response table and child ownership persistence in Evidence section above
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Plugin B forking Plugin A's session (rejected), Plugin B forking ownerless session (rejected), non-plugin client forking any session (allowed), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to Plugin A's session (rejected), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to ownerless session (rejected), Plugin B non-fork parent linking to own session (allowed), Plugin B child has `pluginOwnerId` persisted, Plugin B can reuse its child, Plugin A cannot use Plugin B's child, Plugin B fork child has `pluginOwnerId`, Plugin B parentless create has `pluginOwnerId`
- Edge cases checked: no `pluginRuntimeOwnerId` (skip check), ownerless parent (reject for plugins), self-ownership (allow), `fork === false` with `parentSessionKey` (now gated), child `pluginOwnerId` persistence (fork, non-fork, and parentless)
- What you did NOT verify: Cross-store fork with `targetStorePath`

## Review Conversations

- [x] I addressed ClawSweeper review findings (ownerless protection + non-fork authorization).
- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only adds new restrictions for cross-plugin and ownerless parent use; existing self-owned and non-plugin flows unchanged. This matches existing `sessions.delete` behavior.
- [ ] Config/env changes? No
- [ ] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — the ownership check is placed in `createGatewaySession` at the service layer, close to where the parent session entry is resolved, rather than in the handler. This prevents future callers from accidentally bypassing the check. The unified check (fork + non-fork) mirrors `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` in delete — same rule, same surface.
- **Refactor needed**: No — the check is a self-contained change; `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` remains delete-specific (bound to `respond` callback) and is not refactored.
- **Alternative considered**: Adding the check in the `sessions.create` handler (sessions.ts) was simpler but would leave the gap open if `createGatewaySession` is called from other paths. Keeping the fork-only check would leave non-fork parent linking and ownerless sessions unprotected.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Prompt context included issue body, source-level provenance analysis of `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` and `createGatewaySession`, and ClawSweeper review discussion.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Low risk — this is an additive security hardening that narrows existing behavior. The check mirrors `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` which has been shipping since the delete path. Key mitigations:
- Non-plugin clients (the majority of callers) are entirely unaffected
- Plugin runtimes using their own sessions continue to work
- Ownerless session protection is consistent with existing delete behavior — plugins already cannot delete user sessions
- The error message follows the same pattern as `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch`

**Specific change from earlier PR revision**: The guard was expanded from fork-only to all parent-session use, and ownerless sessions are now protected. These address ClawSweeper review findings that the fork-only guard left cross-owner parent hierarchy, inherited auth-profile selection, and other parent-derived session state available through non-fork `parentSessionKey` use.

Memory search handled blank or whitespace-only queries too late. The manager could initialize the provider, assert provider state, or bootstrap search work before the preflight returned an empty result.

## Why This Change Was Made

Blank query eligibility is a local preflight contract and should not require provider setup. This change shares query normalization with the existing preflight and short-circuits blank queries before provider/bootstrap work.

## User Impact

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Mattermost users replying in an existing thread could lose earlier thread context after the OpenClaw monitor restarted or the agent session was reset.

Fixes #93204

## Why This Change Was Made

The Mattermost monitor now backfills a cold local thread-history window from the Mattermost thread endpoint after inbound admission gates pass. The backfill marker is keyed by the stored thread `sessionId`, not the stable route session key, so a real `/new` or session reset in a thread gets its own recovery fetch while same-session follow-ups avoid repeated server fetches.

When the first cold turn has no stored thread session entry yet, the monitor records a pending backfill marker and adopts it once `recordInboundSessionMeta` creates the stored session id. That keeps the marker stable for same-session follow-ups and failed-fetch no-retry, without blocking a later real session-id rotation.

Recovery is now bounded on both axes flagged in review:

- **Thread response size.** `fetchMattermostThreadPosts` requests only the newest `historyLimit + 1` posts via `?per_page=<limit>&direction=up`, then restores ascending chronological order. `GET /posts/{id}/thread` returns the entire thread by default (Mattermost `per_page=0`), so an unbounded thread would otherwise allocate and parse on the inbound path.
- **Marker lifecycle.** Backfill tracking uses one marker per thread history key (`Map<historyKey, sessionId>`) instead of a process-lifetime `Set` of `historyKey:session` compound keys. Marker memory and lookup cost stay bounded to live threads instead of accumulating an entry per session rotation and scanning the whole set on each candidate. The stored session id is read only after the admission gates, so dropped pre-admission posts never touch the session store.

## User Impact

Mattermost thread replies keep useful prior context after restart or `/new`, without repeated thread-history requests, unbounded thread fetches, or unbounded per-session marker growth on long-lived monitors.

target.title: fix(amazon-bedrock-mantle): dedupe the IAM token-failure diagnostic per region (#67288)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #67288. On hosts with no usable AWS credentials (Raspberry Pi installs, default Docker images), the `amazon-bedrock-mantle` plugin attempts IAM bearer-token generation on every implicit-discovery call (every catalog refresh) and logs `[bedrock-mantle-discovery] Mantle IAM token generation unavailable` **every time** it fails. The user-visible symptom is continuous log noise on installs that never configured AWS.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix dedupes the failure diagnostic per region for the process lifetime instead of gating the IAM chain itself:

- `generateBearerTokenFromIam` keeps running the AWS default credential chain on every call — hosts that rely on late-arriving credentials (instance roles, IRSA, SSO) still start working the moment the chain succeeds, with no opt-in config.
- The `Mantle IAM token generation unavailable` debug line is emitted **at most once per region per process** (`iamTokenFailureLogged` set). A successful token generation for that region clears the marker, so a later regression logs again.

An earlier revision of this PR short-circuited discovery entirely when no AWS env creds were present; that approach was **abandoned after review** because it broke instance-role/IRSA/SSO hosts whose credentials are not visible in env vars. The current diff contains no credential gate and adds no config surface.

**Operator-observability tradeoff (explicit):** for a region that keeps failing, only the *first* failure's details are logged per process. If the underlying failure reason later changes (e.g. from "no credentials" to a network error) while generation keeps failing, the new details are not logged until a token generation succeeds for that region or the gateway process restarts. This trades per-request detail freshness for eliminating unbounded per-request log spam.

## User Impact

- Installs without AWS credentials see the diagnostic once per region instead of on every request.
- Hosts with working or late-arriving IAM chains are unaffected: token generation is still attempted every call.
- No config changes, no new keys, no behavior change for `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` users or explicit `discovery.enabled: false`.

## Evidence

Exact-head (c0e8c4d134b) regression run:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/amazon-bedrock-mantle/discovery.test.ts

 ✓ logs 'IAM token generation unavailable' at most once per region across repeated implicit-discovery calls (#67288)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  34 passed (34)
```

The regression drives the production `resolveImplicitMantleProvider` three times with a failing token provider and asserts, via a captured discovery-subsystem logger, that:
- the token provider factory ran on **all 3** calls (IAM-chain fallback semantics preserved — no short-circuit), and
- the `Mantle IAM token generation unavailable` diagnostic was emitted **exactly once**, with the expected `region` metadata — removing the dedupe guard fails the test.

Not yet supplied: redacted current-head runtime logs from a real credential-less host showing the single diagnostic across repeated catalog refreshes (the remaining reviewer ask).

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Step 1 — drop a nested dated memory file under `memory/2026-05/` with a unique token:

```
cat > ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku/memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md <<'EOF'
Recursive memory search proof.
Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
EOF
```

Step 2 — reindex the live agent's memory store:

```
openclaw memory index
```

Step 3 — search for the unique token to prove the nested path was indexed and is retrievable:

```
openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
```

Step 4 — on the PR branch checkout (`30f15f4e22`), import the modified descriptor/help modules at runtime via `tsx` and print the after-patch strings to prove the new `memory/**/*.md` wording is observable from a real runtime call site (not just the diff):

```
node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs   # imports FIELD_HELP and buildPromptSection from this branch
```

**After-fix evidence**: Terminal output from the installed `openclaw 2026.5.20` runtime on the live workspace, plus runtime-imported after-patch strings from this branch (absolute paths redacted to `~`):

```
$ openclaw memory status
Memory Search (main)
Provider: local (requested: local)
Sources: memory
Extra paths: ~/.openclaw/shared-memory
Indexed: 105/105 files . 933 chunks
Workspace: ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku
By source:
  memory . 105/105 files . 933 chunks
```

```

Memory index updated (main).
```

```
$ openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
[node-llama-cpp] ... falling back to using no GPU
0.812 memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md:1-9
    Recursive memory search proof.
    Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
    This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
    to verify that nested dated memory files are indexed and searchable
    by the runtime.

0.450 memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md:1-6
0.432 memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/pr-draft.md:1-32
```

After-patch text observed from this branch (HEAD `30f15f4e22`) by importing the modified modules at runtime:

```

=== extensions/memory-core/index.ts (post-patch source lines) ===
